wireContractBasis.publish: LIVE-VERIFIED (Lead probe 2026-09-21, account API token, dedicated probe queue zeck-preview-main-executions-probe): {"body": <plain JSON object>} → HTTP 200 with result.metadata.metrics.backlog_count; {"body": "<string>", "content_type": "json"} → HTTP 400 code 10207 (Expected object, received string at body); any {"messages": [...]} wrapper → HTTP 400 (Required at body). Cross-checked against the current public API reference (Push Message, developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/queues/subresources/messages/methods/push, fetched 2026-09-21): request body is the one-of union MqQueueMessageText {body: string, content_type: "text", delay_seconds} | MqQueueMessageJson {body: <json value>, content_type: "json", delay_seconds} — content_type is an enum, delay is expressed in SECONDS. Implementation: the bare body object (live-verified form, the documented default content type json) carrying the port's opaque string payload inside a versioned envelope object {zeckTransport: 1, payload: <string>}; the port's free-form MIME contentType is NOT forwarded (the provider's enum cannot express it); a requested delay rides as delay_seconds.
wireContractBasis.pull: CURRENT-PUBLIC-DOCUMENTED (Pull Queue Messages, developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/queues/subresources/messages/methods/pull + the pull-consumers guide, fetched 2026-09-21) + LIVE-VERIFIED endpoint behavior (Lead probe: pull 405s 'messages cannot be pulled unless http_pull mode is enabled' until the queue carries an http_pull consumer created via POST .../queues/{queue_id}/consumers {"type": "http_pull"} → 200; after that POST .../messages/pull {"batch_size": n} → 200 with result.messages[]): the corrected endpoint is /messages/pull (the stale adapter path was /messages/poll) with {batch_size, visibility_timeout_ms} (documented bounds batch max 100, visibility max 12h — verified against the current limits page). Pull-body delivery form: per the current pull-consumers documentation, json (the default) and bytes content types are delivered BASE64-ENCODED (RFC 4648) over the REST pull surface; text arrives as plain UTF-8. The adapter decodes accordingly (strict RFC 4648 validation; a non-base64 body passes through verbatim — never a silent drop: the authoritative PostgreSQL correlation digest check downstream fails closed on any mismatch) and unwraps its own envelope. The base64 delivery form itself is documentation-verified, NOT live-exercised (the Lead's probe verified the pull endpoint and envelope, not a pulled body) — the Lead's credentialed re-run exercises the full round trip.
wireContractBasis.ack: CURRENT-PUBLIC-DOCUMENTED (Acknowledge + Retry Queue Messages, developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/queues/subresources/messages/methods/ack + the pull-consumers guide's ack example, fetched 2026-09-21): POST .../messages/ack with {"acks": [{"lease_id"}], "retries": [{"lease_id"}]} (a retry entry may optionally carry delay_seconds, which this adapter does not use — a retry re-queues immediately). NOT live-exercised by the Lead's probe (no message remained) — this is the honest verification basis; the shape this adapter has always sent matches the current public schema and examples exactly, so no wire change was needed on this leg.
wireContractBasis.httpPullConsumerProvisioning: LIVE-VERIFIED (Lead probe 2026-09-21) + current public pull-consumers guide: POST /accounts/{account_id}/queues/{queue_id}/consumers {"type": "http_pull"} → 200 (or npx wrangler queues consumer http add <queue-name>); a queue with a push-based Worker consumer must have it removed first. Recorded in deploy/README.md next to the probe-queue requirement.

notes: FINDING F1 (reproduction + root cause + fix + regression pins): reproduction — the Lead's credentialed live probe (2026-09-21) posted the adapter's then-publish shape {"body": "<string>", "content_type": "application/json"} to POST /accounts/{account_id}/queues/{queue_id}/messages and the live API refused it (HTTP 400, provider code 10207, Expected object, received string at body); any {"messages": [...]} wrapper was likewise refused (Required at body); only the BARE object {"body": <plain JSON object>} was accepted (HTTP 200 with result.metadata.metrics.backlog_count). Root cause — adapter defect: the adapter encoded the port's string payload as the wire body VALUE and passed the port's free-form contentType through as content_type, a shape the current Cloudflare Queues REST schema does not accept (body must be an object/array under the json content type; content_type is the enum text|json). Classification: wire-format drift in the owning adapter (src/platform/queue/cloudflare-queues.ts). Fix — publishWire now sends the live-verified bare object with the port payload inside a versioned envelope object ({zeckTransport: 1, payload: <string>}); content_type is no longer forwarded (the enum cannot express a MIME string); a requested delay rides as delay_seconds (the current schema field; the stale shape multiplied into delay_ms); pullWire targets /messages/pull (the current documented endpoint; the stale path was /messages/poll) with unchanged batch/visibility semantics; the pull-body normalization decodes the documented base64 json delivery form and unwraps the envelope (strict RFC 4648 validation; non-base64 bodies pass through verbatim, governed fail-closed by the downstream correlation digest check); settleWire's ack shape was verified against the current public API reference and is UNCHANGED (it matches). Every fail-closed behavior is preserved exactly: 401/403 permanent, 404 permanent, 429/5xx/405/network transient, bounded retry budgets, credential redaction, error slicing. Regression pins — tests/unit/queue/wire-contract.test.ts (the exact request shapes via a fetch double), tests/integration/queue/cloudflare-protocol.test.ts (the corrected shapes over real HTTP; the fake now refuses the stale shapes exactly as the live API did — string body → 400 code 10207, messages-wrapper → 400 Required at body, free-form content_type → 400 — and pins the http_pull consumer precondition + the live-verified consumer-creation REST call), tests/integration/queue/lib/fake-cloudflare-queues.ts (the corrected protocol mirror: publish one-of union validation, the live 200 publish envelope with result.metadata.metrics, /messages/pull + the 405 refusal + consumers endpoint, base64 json pull bodies, /messages/poll no longer routed).

FINDING F2 (reproduction + root cause + fix + regression pins): reproduction — the Lead's live-preview smoke run executed deploy:smoke --environment preview --branch main against revision 9915be6 with the correctly-provisioned per-branch bucket zeck-preview-main-artifacts reachable; the run's identity document (computed WITH the branch slug) named the bucket zeck-preview-main-artifacts, but probeProviderObjectStore's drift cross-check called computeResourceNames WITHOUT the slug, computed zeck-preview-artifacts, and reported the reachable correctly-named bucket as drift (zeck-preview-main-artifacts != zeck-preview-artifacts) — the artifact-bytes concern read unavailable. Root cause — tool defect: deploy/smoke.ts computed the preview branch slug for the identity document but did not thread it into the provider probes' manifest-computed name comparison (the r2-bucket is a perBranch resource). Classification: state-threading defect in the deploy smoke tool. Fix — runSmokeAttestation computes the slug ONCE before the probes and threads it through probeProviderEnvironment → probeProviderObjectStore → computeResourceNames; the whole file was audited for the same omission (probeLocal computes names for the local environment only, where no preview slug can exist — computeResourceName rejects a slug outside preview — and no other manifest-computed name comparison exists in the smoke). Regression pins — tests/unit/deployment/smoke-naming.test.ts: the per-branch expected name over the real manifest (zeck-preview-main-artifacts with the slug, zeck-preview-artifacts without — the exact pair that produced the false drift), the full runSmokeAttestation('preview', {branch: 'main'}) against a real local object-store endpoint reporting the correctly-named per-branch bucket READY with the identity document carrying the same per-branch name, and the negative (a genuinely mis-named bucket still reads as drift — the fix threads the slug, it does not weaken the check).

Verification-basis honesty: the publish shape and the http_pull consumer precondition are LIVE-verified (the Lead's probe matrix, quoted verbatim in spec/post-release-work-orders/PPR-004.md); the pull endpoint/envelope, the base64 json pull-body delivery form, the delay_seconds field, the content_type enum and the ack shape are CURRENT-PUBLIC-DOCUMENTED (developers.cloudflare.com/api Push Message / Pull Queue Messages / Acknowledge + Retry Queue Messages method pages + the pull-consumers guide + the limits page, all fetched 2026-09-21 from this pod). The ack shape was NOT live-exercised (the Lead's probe had no remaining message to acknowledge) — this is recorded above and in the adapter's source comments; the Lead's credentialed re-run is the live attestation for every leg.
